payload.statement:
# Problem: Council review of Chapter 10, Magic System (quarto-book/chapters/10-magic-system.qmd)

You are the hol-rulebook council. Audit this chapter as a publishable unit of the Heroes of Legend
TTRPG rulebook and produce a tiered disposition plan. Do NOT fix anything; file findings only.
One topic: **t-01, "Is Chapter 10 publishable as-is? If not, what is the tiered disposition plan?"**
Refute means it is not publishable as written (state the defect and the minimal fix). Support means
you checked it and found it publishable. Do not invent defects to look thorough: a chapter with few
real problems is a GOOD outcome, and the spine being clean is a finding worth stating with evidence.

## Scope
The registered source `10-magic-system` (the chapter's .qmd, 138 lines, a single `{=typst}` fence).
This chapter is the **framework chapter for magic**: it is the source of record for the always-fires
rule, the one-roll casting model, the tier-to-cost/effect-row table, the Adept/Master level gates,
Discipline prerequisites for spells, cantrips as a category, the arcane-versus-divine tradition
split, the three limitation rules (per-encounter, per-session, concentration), and one worked
example. It is NOT the spell list: the actual spell cards live in ch11 (arcane) and ch12 (divine),
and their names, damage rows, Discipline counts and Keywords are canon there.

Because it is a framework chapter, its blast radius is cross-chapter: anything it asserts about
tiering, gates, prerequisites, wildcards, cantrips, or the tradition split must agree with the
chapters that implement it. Cross-check only against the authoritative chapters: attributes ch03,
disciplines/taxonomy/rank costs/prereq shapes/damage budget ch08, the arcane spell cards and
cantrips ch11, the divine spell cards and cantrips ch12, class discipline pools and signatures ch05
(and the ch02 templates), the Odd's wildcard signature ch05:287 / ch02:301 / ch21:81, core
resolution and the tier bands ch06, combat, conditions and resistance math ch13, equipment ch15,
armor ch16, advancement and the DP economy ch18, GM guidance and the card-format examples ch19,
the bestiary's NPC spell notes ch20, and the glossary ch21.

## Locked conventions the chapter must satisfy (cite the violated convention in every finding)
- **Damage budget is FLAT, keyed to tier.** Novice 2/4/6, Adept 6/9/12, Master 9/15/21 on
  Weak/Standard/Strong. No damage dice anywhere. Every damaging or healing number this chapter
  prints, including inside a worked example, must land on the row for the card's rank. A rider or
  a centre bonus that lands OFF the row (for example a Strong-row number appearing as a bonus on an
  Adept card) is a defect: riders must sum to the row, or gate on the WEAK result so base plus rider
  equals a row, or be a damage TIER bump phrased "+1 damage tier".
- **One-roll principle:** the casting roll IS the effect roll. The 3d6 roll plus attribute plus
  skill maps directly onto Weak (1-8) / Standard (9-14) / Strong (15-18+). No separate casting
  check, no spell-failure roll, no concentration roll that replaces the outcome mapping. Recompute
  every worked roll: attribute plus skill plus dice must produce the tier the example claims.
- **Card costs are flat 2/4/8 DP at Novice/Adept/Master for every class.** Gates: Adept at Level 3,
  Master at Level 7. No class varies them and no spell card varies them.
- **Prerequisite shapes:** a spell card's tier equals the number of Discipline ranks it requires.
  Novice = 1 rank, Adept = EXACTLY 2 ranks (2 different or 2 same), Master = EXACTLY 3 ranks (3
  different, 2+1, or 3 same). No single Discipline may exceed rank 3. A Master card may never be a
  single rank. Wildcards: the Odd's *Eccentric Spellcasting* lets exactly two chosen abilities
  (one arcane, one divine) ignore Discipline prerequisites, level gates still applying. Any blanket
  claim in this chapter that no wildcard or substitution exists contradicts a shipped class
  signature and is a defect.
- **Tier-to-effect consistency:** a card bought at Novice rank uses the Novice row; the same card
  bought up to Adept rank uses 6/9/12; at Master rank, 9/15/21. Whatever this chapter's table and
  prose say the row is must match what the actual add-on lines in ch11/ch12 print.
- **Leveled condition vocabulary.** Conditions use the leveled form (Burning 3, Slowed 5, Dazed 1,
  Asleep 2, Frozen X) as ch13's condition table defines them, or the exact binary name (Prone,
  Frightened, Restrained, Blinded, Dazed, Hidden). Bespoke paraphrases ("takes ongoing fire damage",
  "half Speed", "slowed for 1 round" with no level) are defects. Resistance and vulnerability
  resolve as half and double (ch13).
- **ZERO numeric roll modifiers (Boon/Bane law).** A situational bonus or penalty to a ROLL is Boon
  or Bane, never +N or -N. Numbers are reserved for damage, HP, DR, DP, ranges and durations, plus
  three named exceptions: attributes and skill tiers (Novice +1, Adept +2, Master +3), the DA's
  difficulty dial, and a Challenge penalty. Boons and Banes cancel one for one; the potence ladder
  is Boon/Bane 1 = 4d6 keep three, 2 = 5d6, 3 = 6d6, capped at three.
- **Zero em-dashes in book text (style law, book-wide).** Also zero en-dashes used as dashes.
- **Cross-references:** every @sec-* / @tbl-* / @fig-* token must resolve to a real label, and no
  typed period may follow a cross-reference. A bare `@` in prose is a build breaker.
- **Typst conventions (MIGRATION-SPEC):** exactly one `{=typst}` fence per file with the `# H1` line
  kept above it; callout bodies in the NAMED `body: [...]` form (the positional form is silently
  dropped by the theme and the build still passes); every `#table(` carries `outlined: false`;
  `#label("sec-...")` on the line after its heading. Every `#pagebreak()` must not leave an orphan
  blank page or strand a heading at a page foot.
- **Book-wide conventions that are NOT defects (do not re-flag these):** the `_Figure N.M: Title_`
  placeholder caption where N carries the book's global figure offset (ch08 prints 10.1, ch09 11.1,
  ch10 12.1, ch11 13.1) and is followed by `_Placeholder for final art._`; the absence of a Duration
  header field on card stat blocks; the DA / GM vocabulary split; the intentionally duplicated class
  starting-Discipline listing in ch05 and ch08.
- **Phantom cards and canon:** any spell or ability this chapter names must exist under exactly that
  name in ch11 or ch12, and any number it prints for that card must match the card. A worked example
  is a claim about the printed card, so it must be recomputed against the card, not against memory.
- **Scope-adjacent:** a defect whose only fix site is a DIFFERENT chapter (a stale reference in
  ch08, a wrong pointer in ch19) is still a finding, but label it clearly as routed out so it is not
  implemented inside this chapter's micro-PR.

## Findings format (one finding per member this round)
Each finding must be decision-oriented and carry, in the argument: the broken value with
[10-magic-system:LINE], the expected or correct value, the violated convention, and the minimal fix.
Cite cross-chapter canon lines where the expected value is canon-determined (ch08 for the budget,
ladder, rank costs and prereq shapes; ch11/ch12 for the card text; ch05/ch02/ch21 for the Odd's
signature; ch13 for conditions and resistance). Recompute every number you check: a roll, a tier,
a cost, a Discipline count and a damage row must all agree with each other and with the chapters
that implement them. Verify a card name in another chapter before asserting a phantom. A finding
that cannot state the broken value and the expected value is not a finding. Do NOT invent defects
to look thorough.

## Wall discipline (mandatory)
Paraphrase in `argument` and `evidence[].claim`; keep verbatim text ONLY in
`evidence[].quote_or_excerpt` (<= ~12 words). Never copy 10 or more consecutive words from this
problem statement or from the source chapter into `argument` or `claim`.

Verdict: not publishable as written. One blocking cross-chapter contradiction, two canon-alignment defects, and one wording clash; the numeric spine is otherwise sound, so the repair set is small.

TIER 1 (blocking) [10-magic-system:65] denies outright that a required Discipline can ever be swapped. Broken value: that blanket denial. Expected: the chapter names the one shipped exception, since the Odd's level-1 signature exempts two chosen abilities, one arcane and one divine, from Discipline prerequisites while the level gates still bind (05-classes.qmd:287, 02-character-creation.qmd:301, 21-glossary.qmd:81), and combat plays that rule live when Lyra casts Ember Lance with no Fire rank (13-combat.qmd:498). Violated convention: the prerequisite-shape clause on wildcards. Minimal fix: one sentence crediting the Odd's signature as the sole substitution.

TIER 2a (numbers) [10-magic-system:133] states an Adept spell's Strong result as 12, then gives nearby targets 15. Brimstone Burst is Adept at 2 Fire, so its row is 6/9/12 (08-disciplines.qmd:228-230), and 15 is a Master-row figure; the canonical card carries no centre bonus at all (11-arcane-spells.qmd:136-147). Broken value: the added 15. Expected: every printed number lands on the row for the card's rank. Violated convention: flat, tier-keyed damage budget. Minimal fix: drop the 15 so the centre also takes 12, or recast the extra as an on-row rider or a damage-tier bump.

TIER 2b (tradition split) [10-magic-system:99] enumerates the arcane Disciplines as Fire, Wind, Water, Earth and Energy, but arcane canon also gates spells and a class ability on Mind (11-arcane-spells.qmd:391, 11-arcane-spells.qmd:402, 11-arcane-spells.qmd:415, 05-classes.qmd:538, 05-classes.qmd:172), and Plants runs through both tradition chapters (11-arcane-spells.qmd:280, 12-divine-spells.qmd:330) while 10-magic-system:99-101 names it in neither list. Expected: the two lists cover what the implementing chapters actually use. Violated convention: the arcane-versus-divine split must agree with the chapters that implement it. Minimal fix: add Mind (and Plants) to the arcane list and Plants to the divine list, or mark both lists non-exhaustive.

TIER 3 (wording) [10-magic-system:29] promises there is no concentration roll, yet [10-magic-system:115] then mandates a Fortitude check to keep a spell up after damage. The later check is itself legitimate, it does not replace the casting outcome mapping, so the defect is the absolute promise. Minimal fix: narrow line 29 to the casting roll.

VERIFIED CLEAN (checks run): flat 2/4/8 DP costs and the Level 3 / Level 7 gates match 08-disciplines.qmd:144-146; the 1/2/3 prerequisite counts, the rank-3 ceiling and the three Master shapes match 08-disciplines.qmd:199-208; cantrips with no prerequisite match 11-arcane-spells.qmd:27; the example's three effect-row lines reproduce Ember Lance and Brimstone Burst including Piercing 3 and the 20-ft radius (11-arcane-spells.qmd:126-134, 11-arcane-spells.qmd:139-145); the casting attributes agree with the class keys (05-classes.qmd:148 for the Arcanist, 05-classes.qmd:193 for the Shepherd); Arcana is a real Knowledge-keyed skill (07-skills.qmd:167); the per-encounter cap on Adept spells matches 20-bestiary.qmd:146; both named spells exist under exactly those names (11-arcane-spells.qmd:123, 11-arcane-spells.qmd:136) so neither is a phantom; and the worked roll recomputes to the tier the prose claims (5+3+4 = 12, plus Knowledge +2 and Arcana +1 = 15, Strong per 06-core-resolution.qmd:32, with the stated Standard difficulty being the +0 rung of 06-core-resolution.qmd:220). Typst layer: a single {=typst} fence under the H1, label on the following line, both tables carrying outlined:false, the callout in the named body: form, zero em-dashes or en-dashes (regex search returned nothing), and no dangling cross-reference tokens because the chapter prints none. The 12.1 figure caption is the sanctioned global-offset placeholder.

TIERED DISPOSITION: execute Tier 1 and Tier 2a inside this chapter's micro-PR, since both change reader-usable rules; Tier 2b is a short alignment edit in the same PR; Tier 3 is optional polish. No other change is warranted.

payload.argument:
Refute. Chapter 10 is not publishable as written: seven counter-examples survive recomputation, and three of them are cross-chapter contradictions rather than wording nits.

(1) Off-budget example value. [10-magic-system:133] says an Adept Brimstone Burst deals 12 and adds 15 for foes near the centre. The card prints one row for that tier, 6/9/12 (ch11:143), matching the Adept budget row (ch08:229); 15 is the Master Strong number, so a 4 DP Adept purchase delivers the 8 DP row's peak. Expected value 12. Minimal fix: strike the centre bonus, or re-express it as a damage tier bump.

(2) False blanket ban on wildcard substitutions. [10-magic-system:65] denies that any substitution exists, but the Odd's signature lets two chosen abilities skip Discipline prerequisites (ch05:287, ch02:301, ch21:81), only the level gates survive, and canon play depends on it (ch13:498, Lyra fires Ember Lance holding no Fire rank). Minimal fix: add the class-signature carve-out.

(3) Self-contradicting concentration rule. [10-magic-system:29] promises no concentration roll; [10-magic-system:115] then demands a Fortitude check to keep a maintained spell up after damage lands. Both cannot stand. Minimal fix: reword line 29 so it forbids only a separate casting check and a spell-failure percentage, leaving the maintenance check intact.

(4) Incomplete tradition lists. [10-magic-system:99] defines arcane magic as five forces and [10-magic-system:101] defines divine magic as four, yet ch11 ships arcane cards keyed to Plants (ch11:280, Venom Lance) and Mind (ch11:391 and four more), and ch12 ships a Plant Spells section (ch12:326, Briar Wall). Minimal fix: name Plants and Mind in the arcane list and Plants in the divine one, or reclassify those cards.

(5) Free, unlimited, roll-free cantrips. [10-magic-system:89] hands every caster all cantrips free and at will with no roll mandated, while ch02:145, ch08:214 and ch19:605 price each no-prereq Novice basic, cantrips included, at 2 DP. A starting Arcanist therefore receives ten cantrips the book prices at 20 DP, and since no roll is required while each printed cantrip lists three tiers (ch11:49, Frost Touch), a player can simply claim the Strong line every round. Minimal fix: pick one rule, free or 2 DP each, and state whether cantrips roll.

(6) Unpriced rank upgrade. [10-magic-system:39] binds cost and effect row together in the tier table, but [10-magic-system:55] lets a Novice purchase use the 6/9/12 and 9/15/21 rows without ever naming an upgrade price, so a 2 DP buy can reach the top row. Minimal fix: charge the target tier's flat cost (4 or 8 DP) and say whether the original 2 DP credits.

(7) Unresolved precedence. [10-magic-system:111] caps Adept and Master casting at one use per fight; [10-magic-system:113] caps Master casting per session; no line says which governs when both bite, so a rules-lawyer reads line 111 as permitting a Master spell in every fight of the night. Minimal fix: state that the session cap supersedes.

Tiered disposition. Tier 1, blocking, patch inside this chapter: items 1, 3, 6, 7 (the example and the limitation rules). Tier 2, cross-chapter contradiction, fix here or route: items 2, 4, 5, with item 5's price conflict routed to ch08 if the free grant is kept. Tier 3, routed out only: none whose sole fix site is another chapter.

Verified clean, and how: the tier table (2/4/8 DP, 1/2/3 ranks, gates level 1/3/7) matches ch08:144-146 and ch08:227-231; the printed rows for Ember Lance (2/4/6), Brimstone Burst (6/9/12) and Master Ember Lance (9/15/21, Piercing 3) match ch11:126-128, ch11:139-143 and ch11:134; the example's dice 5+3+4=12 plus Knowledge 2 plus Arcana 1 lands 15 in the top band per ch06:29-32; unlimited Novice casting plus a per-encounter Adept cap match the Archmage block ch20:144-146; the rank-3 ceiling matches ch08:208; and the file carries one typst fence with outlined:false tables, no dash characters and no bare @.

Second, [10-magic-system:29] promises no concentration roll, while [10-magic-system:115] orders a Fortitude check to sustain concentration after damage. Broken value [10-magic-system:115]: the mandatory maintenance check. Expected: one concentration rule, not two. Violated convention: the one-roll principle, which line 29 itself states. Minimal fix: add Mind, Plants and the Intellect, or mark both lists illustrative. Disposition tiers: defects 1 and 2 are substantive cross-chapter corrections, defect 3 is mechanical and local to the example, defects 4-6 are one-line completeness or notation edits. payload.rationale: Topic t-01 closed as a terminal reject by deterministic majority, not by a judgment call: the round-1 engine check returned refute 7, support 0, reject_quorum 4, impasse false, un_rebutted_refutes f-001..f-007, and ruled_topics [], so no judge was convened, no ruling was sealed, and rulings_applied is empty. The seven refutes converge rather than conflict. All seven independently flag the same two cross-chapter contradictions: [10-magic-system:65] denies any wildcard Discipline substitution while the shipped Odd signature Eccentric Spellcasting (05-classes.qmd:287, 02-character-creation.qmd:301, 21-glossary.qmd:81) exempts two chosen abilities and is played live at 13-combat.qmd:498; and [10-magic-system:133] gives an Adept Brimstone Burst a 15-point centre bonus that is off the Adept row 6/9/12 (08-disciplines.qmd:228-230) and absent from the canon card (11-arcane-spells.qmd:143, 19-gm-guidance.qmd:571). Six flag the [10-magic-system:29] versus [:115] concentration contradiction; five or six flag the incomplete arcane/divine enumerations at [:99] and [:101]; four flag the cantrip-pricing split (08-disciplines.qmd:214, 02-character-creation.qmd:145, 19-gm-guidance.qmd:604 versus 11-arcane-spells.qmd:27 and 12-divine-spells.qmd:27) and the unstated raise cost; two flag the [:74] '1 Fire, rank 3' notation against 08-disciplines.qmd:208; and the layout-expert independently reproduced the [:69] column overflow in the built PDF (page 161 renders 'Ember Lance (Master rank)' as 'Ember / Lance (Mas- / ter rank)'). Dissent was weighed as counter-signal, not opposition: every member also reports the numeric and taxonomic spine clean, and those checks are recorded as CLEARED and not re-opened. Where a member's severity label exceeded the evidence (the librarian called [:65] a blocking chapter-local Tier-1 fix) the finding was kept and the tier corrected, because the same false absolute sits at 08-disciplines.qmd:265 and the carve-out cites a shipped class signature. Where a member's fix exceeded canon (the researcher adding 'the Intellect' to the arcane list from ch05:507/526) the sub-claim was partially dismissed, since no arcane card keys to an Intellect Discipline. The three Tier-3 items are genuinely underdetermined by the current text, so each is resolved with a recommended default anchored on locked rulings (flat 2/4/8 DP card pricing; the one-roll 3d6 outcome mapping) and left veto-able by the lead designer.
payload.recommendation: VERDICT: TERMINAL REJECT of topic t-01, 'Is Chapter 10, Magic System publishable as-is, and if not what is the tiered disposition plan?' The deterministic round-1 tally stands at refute 7, support 0, reject_quorum 4, impasse false, with all seven refutes (f-001..f-007) un-rebutted and ruled_topics empty. No judge was convened and no ruling was sealed, so rulings_applied is []. Chapter 10 is NOT publishable as written. CLEARED (verified clean by the members and not to be re-opened): the tier table's flat 2/4/8 DP costs, 1/2/3 Discipline counts and 2-4-6 / 6-9-12 / 9-15-21 effect rows against 08-disciplines.qmd:144-146 and 228-230; the Level 3 / Level 7 gates; Knowledge for arcane and Reason for divine against 03-attributes.qmd:98-100; the three outcome bands against 06-core-resolution.qmd:30; the worked roll recomputes to Strong (5+3+4=12, plus Knowledge +2, plus Arcana +1 = 15); both named spells exist under exactly those names, so neither is a phantom; the per-encounter cap against 20-bestiary.qmd:146; and the whole Typst layer (one {=typst} fence under the H1, outlined:false tables, named callout body, zero em/en-dashes, no bare @, heading levels unskipped, 8 page breaks yielding 9 consecutive pages with no blank page or stranded heading). resolved.outcome: TIER 1 MECHANICAL (chapter-local, no mechanics change) - [10-magic-system:133]: the worked example gives an Adept Brimstone Burst's Strong result a 15-point centre bonus, but the card was bought at Adept tier and its row is 6/9/12 (08-disciplines.qmd:228-230), 15 is a Master-row number, and the canon card prints no centre bonus (11-arcane-spells.qmd:143, 19-gm-guidance.qmd:571). Minimal fix: strike 'with targets near the center taking 15' (or restate it as '+1 damage tier') so every printed figure lands on the Adept row. Flagged by all seven.

TIER 1 MECHANICAL - [10-magic-system:69]: the spell table's columns (12.96%, 11.11%, 27.78%, 48.15%) give the Spell column about 0.61 in of usable width, so built PDF page 161 breaks 'Ember Lance (Master rank)' across three lines and hyphenates it mid-word. Minimal fix: rebalance to columns: (26%, 11%, 24%, 39%), keeping the align arity and trailing comma; sibling 08-disciplines.qmd:117 gives its equivalent lead column 34.15%. Verified against the built PDF by the layout-expert.

TIER 1 MECHANICAL - [10-magic-system:45] versus [:71]: the two table headers disagree on casing and wording ('Effect row' vs 'Effect Range', sentence case vs title case) and both abbreviate the three outcome words and Requirement to W / S / St with no key, while [:73] and [:133] disagree on unit style (20-ft vs 20-foot). Minimal fix: use one header wording, spell the outcome words out as 08-disciplines.qmd:227 does (or add a short key), and unify the radius unit. Flagged by the layout-expert and the author.

TIER 1 MECHANICAL - [10-magic-system:74]: the Master prerequisite prints as '1 Fire, rank 3' where the sibling rows print '1 Fire' and '2 Fire', and canon renders a Fire-only Master requirement as '3 Fire' (08-disciplines.qmd:208). Minimal fix: print '3 Fire', matching the tier-equals-rank-count convention. Flagged by the researcher and the game-architect.

TIER 2 SUBSTANTIVE / CROSS-CHAPTER - [10-magic-system:65]: the blanket claim 'There are no wildcard Discipline substitutions' is false; the Odd's shipped Eccentric Spellcasting exempts exactly two chosen abilities, one arcane and one divine, from Discipline prerequisites while level gates still bind (05-classes.qmd:287, 02-character-creation.qmd:301, 21-glossary.qmd:81) and 13-combat.qmd:498 plays it live. Minimal fix: one sentence naming Eccentric Spellcasting as the sole carve-out (not deleting the rule). The identical false absolute at 08-disciplines.qmd:265 is routed out of this chapter's micro-PR and fixed in the same pass. Flagged by all seven.

TIER 2 SUBSTANTIVE / CROSS-CHAPTER - [10-magic-system:29] versus [:115]: line 29 promises 'no concentration roll' while line 115 mandates a Fortitude check to maintain a concentration spell after damage; the later check is legitimate and does not replace the casting outcome mapping, so the absolute at 29 is the defect. Minimal fix: scope line 29 to the casting roll (no separate casting check, no spell-failure percentage) and keep the single maintenance rule in Limitations. While there, complete the [:115] procedure per the editor-in-chief: state the target (Standard or better on 3d6 + Fortitude), the success tier and the repeat-on-each-damaging-hit rule; the glossary already canonises the save at 21-glossary.qmd:127. Flagged by six.

TIER 2 SUBSTANTIVE / CROSS-CHAPTER - [10-magic-system:99] and [:101]: the arcane list names Fire, Wind, Water, Earth and Energy but omits Mind, which keys arcane cards at 11-arcane-spells.qmd:391 and a class ability at 05-classes.qmd:538; the divine list omits Plants, which keys 12-divine-spells.qmd:330; and Plants also keys an arcane card at 11-arcane-spells.qmd:280. Minimal fix: add Mind and Plants to the arcane list and Plants to the divine one, or explicitly mark both lists non-exhaustive. (The researcher's further request to name 'the Intellect' is not adopted: it is a class ability pool, not an arcane Discipline key.) Flagged by five or six.

TIER 2 SUBSTANTIVE / CROSS-CHAPTER - cantrip pricing: [10-magic-system:89], 11-arcane-spells.qmd:27 and 12-divine-spells.qmd:27 make cantrips free and automatic, while 08-disciplines.qmd:214, 02-character-creation.qmd:145 and 19-gm-guidance.qmd:604 price every no-prereq Novice basic, cantrips included, at 2 DP, so a starting Arcanist would receive ten cantrips the book prices at 20 DP. Minimal fix: reconcile all six sites to one rule; the recommended default (Tier-3 item b) keeps cantrips free and automatic, so the correction lands in the pricing chapters (08-disciplines.qmd:214, 02-character-creation.qmd:145, 19-gm-guidance.qmd:604) rather than here. Flagged by four.

TIER 2 SUBSTANTIVE / CROSS-CHAPTER - [10-magic-system:89] and the prerequisites section: the chapter carries zero outbound cross-reference tokens and sends readers to 'its spell chapter' in prose, so the framework never routes a reader to the chapters it summarises. Minimal fix: add @sec-chapter-arcane-spells and @sec-chapter-divine-spells at [:89] and @sec-chapter-disciplines (or the damage-budget table label) at the tier table and the prerequisites section, naming ch11 and ch12 explicitly. Flagged by the editor-in-chief, the layout-expert, the author and the librarian.

TIER 2 SUBSTANTIVE / CROSS-CHAPTER - de-duplication at [10-magic-system:13-15] and the callout at [:118-120]: the opener reprints sentences already at 01-introduction.qmd:215 and 05-classes.qmd:184 (the 'never useless / never out of options' pair, the spotlight rationale, the 'three times before lunch' punchline), making this the third printing of the same set piece. Minimal fix: cut the opener to one original sentence and cross-reference ch01; retarget the callout's rationale to the per-session rule it actually explains. Also qualify [:37] 'Every spell is a single growing card', which overreaches because cantrips have no tiers. Flagged by the author (adopted with the editorial sub-fixes).

TIER 3 DESIGN-DECISION (implement the recommended default, log as veto-able) - raise-cost at [10-magic-system:55]: the chapter says the tier sets both cost and effect row and that a card grows, but never states what raising an already-bought card costs, so a reader cannot tell whether lifting a Novice (2 DP) card to Master costs the full 8 DP or only the difference. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: raising a card costs the DIFFERENCE toward the target tier's flat price, so the total paid equals the target tier price (2 DP more from Novice to Adept, 4 DP more from Novice to Master, 6 DP more from Adept to Master), and any newly required Discipline ranks are bought separately at their own cost. Rationale: the locked economy prices a card flat 2/4/8 DP by tier (08-disciplines.qmd:144-146), so a difference payment lands the total exactly on the tier price and keeps 'the row is the law' coherent. Flagged by the contrarian, the editor-in-chief, the game-architect and the librarian.

TIER 3 DESIGN-DECISION (implement the recommended default, log as veto-able) - cantrip roll resolution at [10-magic-system:89]: the chapter says no roll is required unless a cantrip says otherwise, yet every printed cantrip carries Weak / Standard / Strong lines (11-arcane-spells.qmd:49 and following), which lets a player always claim the Strong line. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: cantrips stay free and automatic to learn and use for every caster of a tradition, and when an outcome actually matters they resolve on the same single 3d6 casting roll the rest of the book uses (attribute plus skill, mapped to Weak / Standard / Strong per 06-core-resolution.qmd:30), which closes the always-claim-Strong exploit without adding a second check. Rationale: this honours the locked one-roll principle while preserving the free-and-automatic cantrip grant. Flagged by the contrarian, the editor-in-chief, the game-architect and the researcher.

TIER 3 DESIGN-DECISION (implement the recommended default, log as veto-able) - limitation precedence at [10-magic-system:111] versus [:113]: [:111] caps Adept and Master spells at once per combat while [:113] caps Master spells at once per session, and no line states which governs when both bite, so the tighter reading is unclear. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: the per-session Master cap is the tighter limit and governs when both apply, so a Master spell is at most once per session even across multiple fights, while Adept spells remain once per encounter. Rationale: the callout's own rationale at [:118-120] describes the Master cap as spotlight management 'once', and the Archmage block corroborates the once-per-fight cap at 20-bestiary.qmd:146. Flagged by the contrarian and the editor-in-chief.
